agenda_text:
REVISED – Item No. 1-A

  CITY COUNCIL OF MONTEREY PARK
  THE CITY COUNCIL ACTING ON BEHALF OF THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY OF THE FORMER
 REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY, THE HOUSING AUTHORITY, THE MONTEREY PARK FINANCING
  AUTHORITY AND THE MONTEREY PARK GEOLOGIC HAZARD ABATEMENT DISTRICT
  AGENDA

  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MONTEREY PARK CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  320 W. NEWMARK AVENUE, MONTEREY PARK, CA 91754

  Wednesday
  March 5, 2025
  6:30 p.m.

  MISSION STATEMENT
  The mission of the City of Monterey Park is to provide excellent service, foster growth
  and opportunity, and create a joyous and collaborative environment.

  LAND ACKNOWLEDGMENT
  We would like to acknowledge that the land we inhabit today was once known as
  Tovangaar, the home of the Gabrieleño-Tongva people. We show our respect to the
  Gabrieleño-Tongva people, as well as all Indigenous people, past, present, and future,
  and honor their labor as original caretakers of this land. We commit to uplifting the
  Gabrieleño-Tongva people, invite you to acknowledge the history, and join us in caring
  for this land.

GENERAL INFORMATION
Documents related to an Agenda item are available to the public in the City Clerk’s Office located at 320
West Newmark Avenue, Monterey Park, CA 91754, during normal business hours and the City’s website
at www.montereypark.ca.gov/AgendaCenter/City-Council-17.

The public may watch the meeting live on the city’s cable channel MPKTV (AT&T U-verse, channel 99
or Charter Communications, channel 182) or by visiting the city’s website at
www.montereypark.ca.gov/133/City-Council-Meeting-Videos. Per the Americans with Disabilities Act, if
you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please call City Hall at (626) 307-1359 for
reasonable accommodation at least 24 hours before a meeting. Council Chambers are wheelchair
accessible.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION
You may speak up to 5 minutes on an/each Agenda item. You may combine up to 2 minutes of time with
another person’s speaking. No person may speak more than a total of 10 minutes. The Mayor and City
Council may change the amount of time allowed for speakers. Written Communication will be accepted
up  to  24  hours  before  the  meeting  by  completing  an  online  form  at
www.montereypark.ca.gov/writtencomm.

While all comments are welcome, the Brown Act does not allow the City Council to take action on any
item not on the agenda. The Council may briefly respond to comments after Public Communications is
closed. Persons may, in addition to any other matter within the City Council's subject-matter jurisdiction,
comment on Agenda Items at this time. If you provide public comment on a specific Agenda item at this
time, however, you cannot later provide comments at the time the Agenda Item is considered.
   Monterey Park City Council Agenda, March 5, 2025 - Page 2

FLAG SALUTE  The Monterey Park Fire Explorers

  CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act):
  The City reviewed the environmental impacts of the extension under the California
  Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et seq. “CEQA”) and the
  regulations promulgated thereunder (14 Cal. Code of Regs. §§ 15000, et seq., the “CEQA
  Guidelines”). CEQA Guidelines §§ 15060(c)(2), 15061(b)(3), and 15378 exempt activities that
  will not result in a direct or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment,
  activities where there is possibility that it may have a significant effect on the environment, and
  activities that do not constitute a “project” as defined, respectively. This activity reflects
  administrative changes and policy making. Accordingly, this activity is exempt from further
  review.

3-G.  RECEIVE AND FILE STAFF REPORT SUMMARIZING THE STATUS OF THE EMERGENCY

  (2) Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.
   Monterey Park City Council Agenda, March 5, 2025 - Page 4

3-H.  CONSIDERATION AND POSSIBLE ACTION TO AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER, OR
  DESIGNEE, TO ACCEPT CALIFORNIA LIBRARY ASSOCIATION GRANT FUNDING AND
  APPROPRIATE FUNDING INTO 2024-25 FISCAL YEAR BUDGET
  It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  (1) Authorizing the City Manager, or designee, to accept $4,500 in California Library
  Association grant funding to purchase books;
  (2) Authorize the City Manager to appropriate the $4,500 grant funding into the 2024-25
  Fiscal Year budget; and

[4.]  PUBLIC HEARING

4-A.  ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION IMPLEMENTING THE SMALL BUSINESS ASSISTANCE
  PROGRAM USING COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS AND A
  RESOLUTION TO AWARD A MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING TO THE CHINATOWN
  SERVICE CENTER FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION AND ADMINISTRATION OF THE SMALL
  BUSINESS ASSISTANCE PROGRAM
  It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  (1) Opening the public hearing, taking testimonial evidence, and closing the public hearing;
  (2) Approving the implementation of the Small Business Assistance Program (SBAP) using
  an initial allocation of $200,000 in Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds,
  20% of which would be allocated for program administration, to support local businesses
  facing economic challenges and the lingering effects of the mass shooting tragedy and
  COVID-19 pandemic. Subject to funding availability, the City may allocate additional funds
  to support the program;
  (3) Adopt a resolution to adopt policies and procedures for distributing CDBG funds to qualified
  expenses and businesses and/or property owners participating in the SBAP to ensure
  compliance with all applicable CDBG regulations; and
  (4) Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.
  CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act):
  The City reviewed the environmental impacts of the draft Resolution pursuant to the California
  Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et seq. “CEQA”) and the
  regulations promulgated thereunder (14 Cal. Code of Regs. §§ 15000, et seq., the “CEQA
  Guidelines”). CEQA Guidelines §§ 15060(c)(2), 15061(b)(3), 15378, and 15308 exempt activities
  that will not result in a direct or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the
  environment, activities where there is possibility that it may have a significant effect on the
  environment, activities that do not constitute a “project” as defined, and actions to protect the
  environment, respectively. This activity is for general policies and procedure-making intended to
  promote economic development. Any subsequent construction or development will be evaluated
  separately under the CEQA Guidelines. Accordingly, the draft Resolution is exempt from further
  review.

[5.]  NEW BUSINESS – None.
   Monterey Park City Council Agenda, March 5, 2025 - Page 5

[6.]  CITY COMMUNICATIONS (CITY COUNCIL)

6-A.  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF MONTEREY PARK
  RECOGNIZING MARCH 2025 AS EMPLOYEE APPRECIATION MONTH (AS REQUESTED
  BY MAYOR NGO)

6-D.  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF MONTEREY PARK,

73-46

  MINUTES
  MONTEREY PARK CITY COUNCIL
  FINANCING AUTHORITY (MPFA)
  HOUSING AUTHORITY (MPHA)
  GEOLOGIC HAZARD ABATEMENT DISTRICT (GHAD)
  SUCCESSOR AGENCY (SA)
  REGULAR MEETING
  MARCH 5, 2025

The City Council, the Financing Authority (MPFA), the Housing Authority (MPHA), the
Geologic Hazard Abatement District (GHAD), and the Successor Agency (SA) of the City
of Monterey Park held a Regular Meeting of the Council in the Council Chamber, located
at 320 West Newmark Avenue in the City of Monterey Park, Wednesday, March 5, 2025
at 6:30 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER:
Mayor Ngo called the meeting to order at 6:35 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE: Mayor Ngo led the flag salute. Pledge of Allegiance presented by Civic
Superstar Ethan Mai.

ROLL CALL:
Deputy City Clerk Trang called the roll:

Council Members Present:  Henry Lo, Vinh Ngo, Jose Sanchez, Thomas Wong,
  Elizabeth Yang
Council Members Absent:  None.

ALSO PRESENT: City Treasurer Amy Lee, City Clerk Maychelle Yee arrived at 6:53 p.m.,
City Manager Inez Alvarez, City Attorney Karl Berger, Assistant City Manager Diana
Garcia, Fire Chief Chris Thompson, Police Chief Scott Wiese, Director of Human
Resources and Risk Management Christine Tomikawa, Director of Community
Development Jessica Serrano, Director of Finance Martha Garcia, City Librarian Kristin
Olivarez, Director of Public Works Shawn Igoe, Director of Recreation and Community
Services Robert Aguirre, Economic Development Manager Joseph Torres, Recreation
and Community Services Manager Christina Alatorre, Finance Manager Laura Borjon,
Planning Manager Beth Chow, Senior Planner Eliana Muñoz, Senior Children’s Librarian
LV Fraizer, Recreation and Community Services Supervisor Guillermo Chavez,
Economic Development Specialist Janice Huang, Office Assistant II Michelle Martinez

VIRTUALLY PRESENT: None.

  MISSION STATEMENT
 The mission of the City of Monterey Park is to provide excellent service, foster growth and opportunity,
  and create a joyous and collaborative environment.
  .
   73-47
  March 5, 2025
AGENDA ADDITIONS, DELETIONS, CHANGES AND ADOPTIONS:
City Manager Alvarez announced the Annual Weed Abatement Protest Public Hearing
scheduled for the March 5, 2025 City Council meeting will be continued to the regularly
scheduled City Council meeting of March 19, 2025. She also requested to move Agenda
Item Nos. 1A and 6A to be heard after Public Communications.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS:

  This Item was heard after Presentation Item No. 1A. Council Member Lo left the
  dais at 6:53 p.m. and returned at 6:58 p.m.

  - Mistress Transgender Queen spoke about the Monterey Park Police Department
  (MPPD) and her recommendation of equal hiring opportunities for bilingual
  applicants who speak languages aside from Spanish. She urged the city to hire
  more LGBTQ+ Police Officers within the MPPD and conveyed her advocacy
  towards the LGBTQ+ community.

  - Fredrick Douglas spoke about the 2011 Supreme Court Case Synder v. Phelps,
  referencing the First Amendment of the United States Constitution and
  emphasized the right of free speech without discrimination.

  - Javier Caltenco, Public Information Officer of the United States Small Business
  Administration (SBA), Office of Disaster Recovery and Resilience informed the
  public of low interest federal disaster loans and assistance to
  businesses/homeowners affected by the firestorm in January 2025.

  - Bob Gin and Carol Sullivan from the Library Foundation expressed their
  appreciation to the City Council and residents who attended the Monterey Park
  Fall Classic Gala in October 2024. Mr. Gin talked to the City Council about the
  opportunity to purchase a Library Book Mobile with the money raised from the
  Gala and is currently accepting more donations. Mrs. Sullivan announced that
  the next Gala will be held in October 2025 and publicized tickets available for
  purchase for the City Council.

STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:

  This Item was heard after Agenda Item 6A.

  - Community Development: Economic Development Specialist Huang presented
  a PowerPoint presentation on the updates and events occurring in Monterey
  Park which includes the Meet-Up with the Mayor event and the Women in
  Business Workshop and Networking event. Specialist Huang reminded the public
  about the launch of the Love Monterey Park Shop and Dine Campaign to
  encourage economic growth between local small businesses and shared the
  extension of the of the Taste of Downtown Monterey Park promotion program.
   73-48
  March 5, 2025
  Economic Development Manager Torres recognized 360 Labs, a natural product
  manufacturing company located in Monterey Park and introduced Chief
  Executive Officer David Kerdoon, and Chief Operating Officer Reyner Schindler.
  Mr. Kerdoon alongside Mr. Schindler spoke in gratitude of their time in Monterey
  Park and conveyed their long-term commitment to stay in the City. Mayor Ngo
  alongside the City Council presented a certificate of recognition to 360 Labs and
  expressed comments of appreciation.

  City Manager Alvarez announced the departure of Community Development
  Director Serrano and expressed gratitude for her efforts to improve the City
  throughout the years.

  - Library: Senior Children’s Librarian Frazier provided a PowerPoint presentation
  on the upcoming programs held at the Library including the 2025 Volunteer
  Income Tax Assistance (Vita) Clinic; the Free Legal Assistance Clinic held every
  second Tuesday of the month; the Art Farm program for emerging authors and
  writers; the announcement of Woman’s History Month, where books and media
  written by women creators will be displayed at the Library throughout the month
  and the “We Can Be She-Roes” program.

  - Recreation and Community Services: Recreation and Community Services
  Supervisor Chavez announced updates which included the success of the
  Valentine’s Day Dance and informed the public about the Free Education
  Nutrition Workshop and Health Screening Workshop. He reminded the residents
  to share their opinion on the Monterey Park Mural Project suggestion survey and
  shared upcoming events such as the monthly Disco Dance Party known as
  “Bloom and Boogie”, the National Fine Arts “Art, Music and Fashion Show”
  presented by the Boys and Girls Club, the 25th Annual Cherry Blossom Festival
  and the Spring Break Day Camp. Supervisor Chavez spoke about the return of
  the Farmer’s Market in April, open job applications for Lifeguard positions in the
  City and ended with the announcement of the Spring Egg Hunt at Barnes Park
  and a trip to the Broad Museum provided by the Langley Senior Center.

1.  PRESENTATION:
  The matters listed under presentation are informational content and for discussion
  only.

1-A.  CONGRESSIONAL APP CHALLENGE FINALISTS - DREXEL NGO, ALINA
  RAMOS, EVAN LAU, AND ATHICHA CHANPRADUB

  This Item was heard after Agenda, Additions, Deletions. Changes and Adoptions.

  Drexel Ngo alongside Alina Ramos, Evan Lau and Athicha Chanpradub spoke
  about their free handsfree desktop application, Eyespeak. The app was created
  for individuals with disabilities to navigate the internet using their eyes and speech.
  Drexel shared the team’s plan to publish their application to the public in the future.
   73-49
  March 5, 2025
  Mayor Ngo, alongside the City Council awarded certificates to the finalists and
  shared words of appreciation on their accomplishment.

2.  OLD BUSINESS: None.

3.  CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS NOS. 3A-3H

  All items under the Consent Calendar are considered by the City Council to be
  routine and will be enacted by one motion. Specific items may be removed from
  the Consent Calendar at the request of any member of the City Council for
  separate consideration.

  City Clerk Yee announced public speakers for Agenda Item Nos. 3E and 3F

  Public Speakers:

  - Mistress Transgender Queen spoke on Agenda Item No. 3E about the Housing
  Element Annual Progress Report and expressed her frustrations towards the
  City’s alleged treatment of the homeless, emphasizing respect and the necessity
  for affordable housing in the City of Monterey Park.

  - Fredrick Douglas spoke on Agenda Item No. 3E voicing his discontent about
  affordable housing, claiming it to be unachievable and recommended the City of
  Monterey Park to act and create a plan that will combat the current homeless
  crisis.

  - Mistress Transgender Queen articulated her opinion on Agenda Item No. 3F
  about neighboring cities and the lack of preparation during the wind and
  firestorms of January 2025 and recommended the City of Monterey Park to act
  and prepare for emergency events that may occur in the future.

  Action Taken: The City Council approved and adopted Agenda Item Nos. 3A, 3B,
  3D, 3F, 3G and 3H on Consent Calendar, excluding Agenda Item Nos. 3C and 3E
  which were pulled for discussion, separate motion, reading resolutions and
  ordinances by the title only and waiving further reading thereof. City Manager
  Alvarez declared an amendment to Resolution No. 2025-R11 in Agenda Item 3-D,
  reporting the effective start date of March 5, 2025 for Interim Director of Community
  Development Phillip Lanzafame be amended to March 17, 2025.
   73-50
  March 5, 2025
  Motion: Moved by Council Member Wong and seconded by Council Member Lo,
  motion carried by the following vote:

  Ayes:  Council Members:  Wong, Sanchez, Lo, Yang, Ngo
  Noes:  Council Members:  None
  Absent:  Council Members:  None
  Abstain:  Council Members:  None
  Recusal:  Council Members:  None

3-A.  MINUTES

  It is recommended that the City Council consider approving the minutes from the
  regular meeting of January 15, 2025 and the special meeting of January 21, 2025.

  Action Taken: The City Council approved the minutes from the regular meeting
  of January 15, 2025 and the special meeting of January 21, 2025, on Consent
  Calendar.

3-B.  MONTHLY INVESTMENT REPORT – JANUARY 2025

  As of January 31, 2025, invested funds for the City of Monterey Park total
  $91,257,894.74.

  Action Taken: The City Council received and filed the monthly investment report
  on Consent Calendar.

3-C.  CONSIDERATION AND POSSIBLE ACTION TO ADOPT RESOLUTION
  DECLARING UNCLAIMED MONIES AS PROPERTY OF THE CITY OF
  MONTEREY PARK AND ORDERING IT TRANSFERRED TO THE CITY’S
  GENERAL FUND PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §§ 50050, ET SEQ.

  Adopting the attached Resolution will transfer unclaimed money that has remained
  in the City’s possession for at least three years (one year for unclaimed money in
  an amount that is less than $15) into the City’s General Fund. Unclaimed money
  may be escheated to the City’s General Fund pursuant to Government Code §§
  50050 to 50055, as described in the City’s Administrative Policy No. 20-26
  (Attachment 2, to the staff report), provided that the City first publishes notice in a
  newspaper of general circulation for at least two consecutive weeks.

  Unless claimed or challenged by a verified complaint, the unclaimed monies
  become the property of the City at least 45 days, but no more than 60 days, after
  the initial public notice pursuant to Government Code §§ 50050 and 50051. The
  Finance Director (“Director”) caused notice to be published in the Monterey Park
  Progress newspaper for two consecutive weeks on January 16, 2025, and January
  23, 2025 (the “Notice”). The Director has not received any claims or complaints
  concerning the unclaimed monies.
   73-51
  March 5, 2025
  Action Taken: The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2025-R10 declaring
  unclaimed monies as property of the City of Monterey Park and ordering it
  transferred to the City’s General Fund.

  Motion: Moved by Council Member Wong and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Yang,
  motion carried by the following vote:

  Ayes:  Council Members:  Wong, Sanchez, Lo, Yang, Ngo
  Noes:  Council Members:  None
  Absent:  Council Members:  None
  Abstain:  Council Members:  None
  Recusal:  Council Members:  None

  Resolution No. 2025-R10
  A RESOLUTION DECLARING UNCLAIMED MONIES AS PROPERTY OF THE
  CITY OF MONTEREY PARK AND TRANSFERRING IT TO THE CITY’S
  GENERAL FUND PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE § 50053

3-D.  ADOPTING A RESOLUTION APPOINTING AN INTERIM DIRECTOR OF
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §
  21221(H) AND EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. N-25-20

  The current Director of Community Development, Jessica Serrano, submitted her
  notice of resignation from the City of Monterey Park. On February 14, 2025, the
  City entered into an agreement with City Management Advisors, LLC (formerly
  known as Peckham and McKenney), to conduct the recruitment for the upcoming
  vacant position. Per Government Code 2122(H), the City Council may appoint a
  retired annuitant to an interim position for a department head vacancy as long as
  the following criteria are met: 1) there is an active recruitment for the vacant
  position, 2) the appointment is for a limited duration during the active recruitment,
  3) there is a single appointment once the contract term ends, and 4) compensation
  cannot exceed the maximum hourly rate for the vacant position.

  City staff have connected with a retired annuitant, Philip Lanzafame, who has over
  25 years of experience in Community Development, Economic Development, and
  housing from a nearby Los Angeles County public agency. His technical
  knowledge and experience will provide the Community Development Department
  the support needed to keep projects and daily activities moving forward in a
  seamless manner. Staff recommends the appointment of Mr. Lanzafame to the
  Interim Director of Community Development position.
   73-52
  March 5, 2025
  Action Taken: The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2025-R11 requesting
  appointment for the position of Interim Director of Community Development
  pursuant to Government Code § 2122(H) and Executive Order No. N-25-20 and
  authorized the City Manager to execute an agreement between the City of
  Monterey Park and the Interim Director of Community Development in a form
  approved by the City Attorney, as amended to revise the effective start date of
  March 5, 2025 for Interim Director of Community Development Phillip Lanzafame
  to March 17, 2025 on Consent Calendar.

  Resolution No. 2025-R11
  A  RESOLUTION  REQUESTING APPOINTMENT  PURSUANT  TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE § 21221(H) AND EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. N-25-20 FOR
  THE POSITION OF INTERIM COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR

3-E.  2024 MONTEREY PARK GENERAL PLAN AND HOUSING ELEMENT ANNUAL
  PROGRESS REPORT

  This report is prepared in compliance with California Government Code section
  65400(a)(2), which mandates that the city prepare an annual report on the status
  and implementation of its General Plan. The report must be submitted by April 1 of
  each year to the City Council, OPR, and HCD.

  The 2024 General Plan and Housing Element Annual Progress Report
  summarizes the City’s progress towards implementing the Monterey Park General
  Plan from January 1, 2024, to December 31, 2024. Throughout calendar year
  2024, the City has been continuously implementing the policies and programs that
  help achieve goals contained within the General Plan.

  Discussion: Director of Community Development Serrano introduced Senior
  Planner Muñoz to present Agenda Item No. 3E.

  Senior Planner Muñoz presented a PowerPoint presentation depicting the
  Monterey Park General Plan and Housing Element Report covering calendar year
  2024. She stated discrepancies in the Housing Element Implementation tables
  provided on attachment number 1 to the staff report and ensured staff’s diligence
  to review the accuracy of the data before officially submitting the report to the state.

  Action Taken: The City Council received and filed the 2024 General Plan and
  Housing Element Annual Progress Report and directed the City Manager, or
  designee, to forward a copy of the report to the Governor’s Office of Planning and
  Research (“OPR”) and the State Department of Housing and Community
  Development (“HCD”) before April 1, 2025, on Consent Calendar.
   73-53
  March 5, 2025
  Motion: Moved by Council Member Wong and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Yang,
  motion carried by the following vote:

  Ayes:  Council Members:  Wong, Sanchez, Lo, Yang, Ngo
  Noes:  Council Members:  None
  Absent:  Council Members:  None
  Abstain:  Council Members:  None
  Recusal:  Council Members:  None

  AMENDING THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PLAN AND RECEIVE AND FILE A

3-G. RECEIVE AND FILE STAFF REPORT SUMMARIZING THE STATUS OF THE
  EMERGENCY REPLACEMENT OF FIRE DEPARTMENT SELF-CONTAINED
  BREATHING APPARATUS

  On December 18, 2024, City Council adopted Resolution No. 2024-R98
  authorizing the City Manager to take necessary measures for the emergency
  replacement of self-contained breathing apparatus for the Fire Department. SCBAs
  are critical personal protective equipment for fire suppression staff, and the Fire
  Department’s current inventory is no longer supported for repairs and replacement
  parts as of December 16, 2024. To ensure fire suppression staff are properly
  protected, the current inventory of SCBAs needs immediate replacement.

  The Fire Chief (“Chief”) obtained a quote from Bauer Compressors, Inc. for the
  replacement of SCBAs, which includes both the items and a comprehensive
  service warranty for $633,812.92.

  The City ordered the replacement SCBAs from Bauer Compressors on December
  19, 2024. The Department received the first shipment of SCBAs the second week
  of January 2025, which contained about 30% of the needed SCBAs and parts.
  Bauer confirmed that the remainder of the order is slated to ship out the second
  week of March. Once the full order has been received, the necessary training and
  calibration will take place before the SCBA’s are deployed for use.

  Action Taken: The City Council received and filed this staff report summarizing
  the status of the emergency replacement of self-contained breathing apparatus on
  Consent Calendar.

4-A.  ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION IMPLEMENTING THE SMALL BUSINESS
  ASSISTANCE PROGRAM USING COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK
  GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS AND A RESOLUTION TO AWARD A MEMORANDUM
  OF UNDERSTANDING TO THE CHINATOWN SERVICE CENTER FOR THE
  IMPLEMENTATION AND ADMINISTRATION OF THE SMALL BUSINESS
  ASSISTANCE PROGRAM

  After dissolving redevelopment agencies, the California Legislature adopted
  “Economic Opportunity” legislation in 2014, which allows use of public funds to
  promote economic development (SB 470, Wright 2013). Depending on the type of
  economic development a city is seeking to promote, a city may be required to make
  findings to demonstrate that the use of public funds towards economic
  development initiatives will likely create jobs, improve tax revenues, or satisfy a
  need for affordable housing.

  The City Council’s 2024-2025 Strategic Plan includes a goal to “Strengthen our
  local economy and enhance housing opportunities”. Using elements of the
  Economic Opportunity legislation may help advance this goal.

  The SBAP presents a valuable opportunity to leverage CDBG funding to directly
  support the local business community. By providing targeted financial assistance,
  the program can contribute to the economic recovery, growth, and long-term
  prosperity of Monterey Park.

  CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act):
  The City reviewed the environmental impacts of the draft Resolution pursuant to
  the California Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et seq.
  “CEQA”) and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14 Cal. Code of Regs. §§
  15000, et seq., the “CEQA Guidelines”). CEQA Guidelines §§ 15060(c)(2),
  15061(b)(3), 15378, and 15308 exempt activities that will not result in a direct or
  reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment, activities
  where there is possibility that it may have a significant effect on the environment,
  activities that do not constitute a “project” as defined, and actions to protect the
  environment, respectively. This activity is for general policies and procedure-
  making intended to promote economic development. Any subsequent construction
  or development will be evaluated separately under the CEQA Guidelines.
  Accordingly, the draft Resolution is exempt from further review.

  Public Speakers:

  - Mistress Transgender Queen addressed crimes that directly affect small
  businesses throughout the city and requested more protection from the Monterey
  Park Police Department.

resolution which included the following amendments: remove the verbiage “and

A. He depicted an overview of the Small Business Assistance Program,
emphasizing the program’s goal to contribute to the economic recovery, growth,
and long-term prosperity of Monterey Park.

Chinatown Service Center’s Community Economic Development Manager, John

Action Taken: The City Council (1) opened the public hearing at 8:21 p.m., took

allocation of $200,000 in Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds,

may allocate additional funds to support the program and (3) adopted Resolution
No. 2025-R13 to adopt policies and procedures for distributing CDBG funds to
